summary.text:
The task is to judge the BOOK ENTRY for "Righteousness" against the common interpretation and the scriptural evidence.
{
  "book_core_identification": "Righteousness is right-living: God's commandments lived out by those under His authority; God is Right-Living by definition; opposite is sin.",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [],
  " strongest_counter": "The common interpretation: righteousness primarily means right standing before God (forensic justification/imputation of Christ's righteousness by faith, apart from works), with conformity to God's character as secondary or symbolic.

content.text:
{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The entry's core identification of righteousness as right-living (God by definition; His commandments lived out for those under authority) is the best explanation of the supplied texts. Direct definitional verses (Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172; 1 John 3:7; Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17) name commandments/doing as righteousness itself and identify God as righteous in His ways/works. The Pauline texts (Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9) are accounted for without contradiction once wage/debt claims are distinguished from duty-obedience (Luke 17:7-10; Heb 11:8), so imputed status is gift-source rather than a rival substance. No stronger counter explains the same cross-text pattern with fewer steps.",
  "book_core_identification": "Righteousness is right-living: God is right-living by definition, and for those under His authority it is His commandments lived out (opposite: sin).",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "God is Right-Living by definition",
    "for those under His authority, righteousness is His commandments lived out",
    "Opposite: Sin"
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Broader chapter claims equating the wedding garment strictly with plural righteous acts/deeds that must be woven and washed, or fully collapsing forensic language into conduct alone, go beyond the printed glossary entry",
    "Extended re-readings of 'end of the law', paidagōgos, cheirographon, and armor pieces as exclusively right-living clothing are chapter applications, not glossary assertions"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Righteousness primarily denotes right standing/status before God (especially forensic/imputed righteousness of God/Christ credited by faith apart from works), with moral conformity as secondary fruit rather than the definition itself.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Righteousness is chiefly a conferred legal/relational status of right standing with God received by faith.",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter denies that righteousness is definitionally the living-out of God's commandments (or God's own right-living) and treats commandment-keeping as non-constitutive of the term's primary referent.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Rom 4:4-8 and Phil 3:9 contrast faith-counted/imputed righteousness with law/works righteousness, appearing to locate the term in status rather than deeds",
    "Common readings of 2 Cor 5:21, Rom 3:21-26, and Gen 15:6 as forensic crediting",
    "Traditional Protestant emphasis on alien righteousness as garment/status covering the sinner"
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Directly matches explicit definitional statements (Deut 6:25 'it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do'; Ps 119:172 'all thy commandments are righteousness'; 1 John 3:7 'he that doeth righteousness is righteous')",
    "Unifies God-as-righteous texts (Deut 32:4; Ps 145:17) with human texts under one 'right-living' sense without special pleading",
    "Integrates Rom 4/Phil 3:9 via the supplied wage-vs-duty distinction (Luke 17:10) and faith-that-obeys (Heb 11:8) so the same verses support rather than overturn the core",
    "Opposite 'sin' follows immediately from 1 John 3:4 lawlessness vs. doing righteousness"
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Fits the surface contrast language of 'not having mine own righteousness which is of the law' (Phil 3:9) and 'imputeth righteousness without works' (Rom 4:6)",
    "Aligns with long-standing confessional readings that prioritize justification status"
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Deuteronomy 6:25",
    "Psalms 119:172",
    "1 John 3:7",
    "Deuteronomy 32:4",
    "Psalms 145:17",
    "Romans 4:4-8 (read with Luke 17:7-10 wage/duty distinction)",
    "Philippians 3:9",
    "Hebrews 11:8"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [],
  "confidence": "high"
}

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
